questions.text: What is the first NSCP Section 420.7 rule for embedments in concrete?

options.text: Embedments may reduce fire protection if the contractor approves.
Embedments shall not significantly impair structural strength or reduce fire protection.
Embedments are checked only after occupancy.
Embedments are outside structural review.

rationale.correct: Section 420.7.1 states that embedments shall not significantly impair structural strength and shall not reduce fire protection.
rationale.takeaway: The first filter is structural and fire-protection impact.
rationale.source_boundary: Batch 164 question-alignment remediation uses only the checked local NSCP OCR anchors listed in source-audit-evidence.json.
rationale.a: Not selected: Embedments may reduce fire protection if the contractor approves.
rationale.b: Selected: Embedments shall not significantly impair structural strength or reduce fire protection.
rationale.c: Not selected: Embedments are checked only after occupancy.
rationale.d: Not selected: Embedments are outside structural review.

questions.text: What minimum reinforcement area does NSCP Section 420.7.4 require perpendicular to pipe embedments?

options.text: At least 0.002 times the area of the concrete section.
Exactly the area of the pipe wall.
No perpendicular reinforcement is mentioned.
At least 10 percent of the beam area.

rationale.correct: Section 420.7.4 requires reinforcement with area at least 0.002 times the concrete section area perpendicular to pipe embedments.
rationale.takeaway: The checked anchor gives a reinforcement-area rule for pipe embedments.

rationale.b: Not selected: Exactly the area of the pipe wall.

questions.text: What minimum specified concrete cover is required for pipe embedments and fittings exposed to earth or weather?

options.text: 20 mm
40 mm
75 mm
No cover is specified.

rationale.correct: Section 420.7.5 requires at least 40 mm cover for pipe embedments and fittings in concrete exposed to earth or weather.
rationale.takeaway: Use 40 mm for earth or weather exposure under the checked source.
rationale.source_boundary: Batch 164 question-alignment remediation uses only the checked local NSCP OCR anchors listed in source-audit-evidence.json.
rationale.d: Not selected: No cover is specified.

rationale.takeaway: The checked source distinguishes 40 mm exposure cover from 20 mm protected cover.

questions.text: How must aluminum embedments be handled under NSCP Section 420.7.3?

options.text: They must be coated or covered to prevent aluminum-concrete reaction and electrolytic action between aluminum and steel.
They are prohibited in every concrete member.
They need no protection if fully hidden.
They are treated the same as reinforcing bars.

rationale.correct: Section 420.7.3 requires aluminum embedments to be coated or covered to prevent aluminum-concrete reaction and electrolytic action between aluminum and steel.
rationale.takeaway: The checked rule is protective treatment, not a blanket prohibition.

rationale.b: Not selected: They are prohibited in every concrete member.
rationale.c: Not selected: They need no protection if fully hidden.

questions.text: If an embedment is not shown in the construction documents, what does Section 426.8 require?

options.text: It may be installed without design review.
It shall be submitted for review by the licensed design professional.
It automatically becomes nonstructural.
It is accepted if the pipe is small.

rationale.correct: The checked Section 426.8 continuation states that embedments not shown in construction documents shall be submitted for review by the licensed design professional.
rationale.takeaway: Unshown embedments require design-professional review before acceptance.

questions.text: Before concrete reaches specified strength, what may be placed in embedded pipes under the checked Section 426.8 rule?

options.text: Any gas if the pressure is below the building service pressure.
Only water not exceeding 32 C or 0.35 MPa.
Any liquid if the pipe is coated.
Nothing is ever permitted inside embedded pipes.

rationale.correct: Section 426.8 allows only water not exceeding 32 C or 0.35 MPa before the concrete has attained specified strength.
rationale.takeaway: The checked rule tightly limits pipe contents before concrete reaches specified strength.

questions.text: Where should piping in solid slabs generally be placed, except for radiant heating or snow melting?

options.text: Between top and bottom reinforcement.
Below all reinforcement at the slab soffit.
Outside the concrete section only.
Only inside beams.

rationale.correct: Section 426.8 states that in solid slabs, piping except for radiant heating or snow melting shall be placed between top and bottom reinforcement.
rationale.takeaway: Solid-slab piping is coordinated with the reinforcement layers.

rationale.a: Selected: Between top and bottom reinforcement.
rationale.b: Not selected: Below all reinforcement at the slab soffit.
rationale.c: Not selected: Outside the concrete section only.

questions.text: How must conduit and piping be fabricated and installed relative to reinforcement?

options.text: So reinforcement can be displaced freely in the field.
So reinforcement cutting is decided after concrete placement.
So cutting, bending, or displacement of reinforcement from its specified location is not required.
So reinforcement is omitted wherever pipes pass.

rationale.correct: Section 426.8 requires conduit and piping to be fabricated and installed so cutting, bending, or displacement of reinforcement from its specified location is not required.
rationale.takeaway: Pipe coordination must protect the specified reinforcement layout.
